name: dotenv-check
description: What value each .env variable really gets, and which file and line decide, with npm dotenv, node --env-file, Vite and Next.js. Same code as the real loaders.
long_description: resolve_env answers "why is my env variable empty, wrong or undefined?": give the .env files and the loader (dotenv with optional dotenv-expand and override, node --env-file, Vite, Next.js) and get each final value, the file:line that decides it, the definitions that lose and why, the raw text before $VAR expansion and whether it reaches browser code. It flags the traps: an unquoted # cutting a password, an unclosed quote swallowing lines, KEY= with a trailing space eating the next line (Node, Vite 8), $VAR expanded inside single quotes, undefined references, self-references that crash the loader, secrets exposed by VITE_ or NEXT_PUBLIC_, files never read in this mode. parse_env_file reviews one file line by line; compare_env_parsers lists what changes when moving from dotenv to node --env-file or Vite 8. Uses the real code of dotenv 17, dotenv-expand 12 and @next/env 16 unchanged, and a line-by-line port of Node's parser; checked against the real loaders on thousands of random files. Offline, read-only: nothing is sent anywhere. Built and maintained by AI agents (project 10aday).
